exact_statement_tex: \label{rem:characteristic-two-ample-residual} Suppose that $Y$ is merely ample, with the same characteristic-two equality and torsion hypotheses, and additionally suppose that $X$ has a purely inseparable ruled rational cover of degree two. If the resulting ruling curve $C$ has positive genus, the proof above still gives \[ g(C)=1,\qquad \chi(\OO_X)=K_X^2=c_2(X)=0,\qquad b_1(X)=b_2(X)=2. \] The general-fibre identities give a positive even integer $b=Y\cdot F$. Equation~\eqref{eq:characteristic-two-canonical-square}, before its strict inequality, then forces $b=2$ and $p_a(F)=1$. Moreover, $Y\to B=C^{(2)}$ is separable of degree two. Its degree is $Y\cdot F=2$; if it were inseparable, it would be a relative Frobenius followed by an isomorphism and would preserve genus. That would give $g(Y)=1$, contrary to $g(Y)=Y^2+1\geq2$. Thus the purely inseparable multisection obstruction in Proposition~\ref{prop:quasielliptic-multisection} does not already exclude this configuration. The genus-zero branch for merely ample $Y$ satisfies the necessary numerical conditions in Proposition~\ref{prop:rational-normalization-canonical}. The present proposition concerns the function field of the normalized cover and does not extend a chosen rational ruling map over every point of that cover. It supplies no existence example for the Picard kernel, and does not settle the higher-conductor or strict-inequality cases.

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:residual-adjoint} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral very ample divisor, and let $s$ be its canonical section. Suppose that a nonzero closed global one-form $\omega$ vanishes along $Y$. Let $m$ be its exact order along $Y$, and let $Z$ be the divisorial zero part, with multiplicities, of $\theta=\omega/s^m\in H^0(X,\Omega^1_{X/k}(-mY))$. Then $m=pa$ for an integer $a\geq1$, $Y$ is not a component of $Z$, and \[ 0\leq Z\cdot Y\leq 2g(Y)-2-mY^2. \] The divisor \[ A=K_X-(m-2)Y-Z \] is nef and big, with $A^2>0$. More precisely, the linear system \[ W_K=\{d((u/s)\omega):u\in H^0(X,\OO_X(Y))\} \subset H^0(X,\omega_X) \] has exact fixed divisor $(m-2)Y+Z$ and two-dimensional image. Its residual system has no fixed curve, and on a dense open of $Y$ its rational map is the given hyperplane embedding. The map $u\mapsto d((u/s)\omega)$ has kernel $ks$. In particular, \begin{align*} h^0(X,\Omega^1_{X/k})&\geq h^0(X,\OO_X(Y)),\\ \operatorname{rank}\bigl[d:H^0(X,\Omega^1_{X/k})\to H^0(X,\omega_X)\bigr]&\geq h^0(X,\OO_X(Y))-1,\\ p_g(X)&\geq h^0(X,\OO_X(Y))-1. \end{align*} Both $K_X-(m-2)Y$ and $K_X-(p-2)Y$ are big, and the canonical map of $X$ has two-dimensional image.

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:odd-higher-conductor-equality} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of odd characteristic $p$, let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral very ample curve, and let $M$ be a nontrivial line bundle of order $p$ whose restriction to $Y$ is trivial. Let $\omega$ be its logarithmic form, let $pa$ be its exact vanishing order along $Y$, and let $\pi:N\to X$ be the normalization of its $\mu_p$-torsor. Suppose that \[ 2g(Y)-2=paY^2. \] Put $d=Y^2$. Then $a\geq5$, $N$ is smooth with ample canonical bundle, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-conductor-invariants} \begin{gathered} K_X\sim(pa-1)Y,\qquad K_N\sim(a-1)\pi^*Y,\qquad p\mid d,\\ K_N^2=p(a-1)^2d,\qquad c_2(N)=-pa\,d,\\ 12\chi(\OO_N)=p(a^2-3a+1)d. \end{gathered} \end{equation} Let $f:N\to C$ be its Albanese fibration, let $g$ be its arithmetic fibre genus, and put \[ L=\pi^*Y,\qquad \ell=L\cdot F \] for a general fibre $F$. Exactly the following three rows can survive the canonical divisibility, genus-change and slope bounds: \begin{equation}\label{eq:odd-conductor-three-genera} \begin{array}{c|c|c|c} \ell&\text{range of }a&g&\text{divisibility}\\ \hline 1&a\geq5\text{ odd}&(a+1)/2&p-1\mid a+1\\ 2&a\geq7&a&p-1\mid2a\\ 3&a\geq21\text{ odd}&(3a-1)/2&p-1\mid3a-1 \end{array} \end{equation} The second and third rows require a nonhyperelliptic fibration. exact_statement_tex: [Scope and comparison] \label{rem:boundary-albanese-scope} The curve-pullback bound uses an existing morphism $X\to B$. The curve-pullback bound does not require a fibration arising from the resolved curve of square zero. Proposition~\ref{prop:boundary-resolved-fibration} does produce a separate fibration on a suitable covering resolution, using actual triviality of its normal line and the moving lemma. The elliptic-base case and the inseparable surface-image case in Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-smallest-albanese-gate} remain unresolved by these arguments. Existence of either configuration remains open. The nonclosed one-forms from Proposition~\ref{prop:residual-adjoint} are compatible with rational collinearity: $d(r\omega)$ can be nonzero although all pairwise wedges vanish. For comparison, Cotner--Zavyalov prove a Lefschetz theorem for finite flat commutative coefficients under a Hodge-equivalence or strongly ample hypothesis \cite[Theorem~3.3.5, pp.~1861--1862]{CotnerZavyalov}. Applied to $\mu_2$ and a strongly ample curve on a surface, it gives injectivity of restriction on order-two line bundles. Strong ampleness is an additional hypothesis; their Example~3.3.6 concerns failure for $\alpha_p$ and does not provide an order-two line-bundle example. Our bound instead retains $\deg\omega_{B'}$ in \eqref{eq:boundary-curve-pullback-conormal}. The remaining inseparable Albanese case belongs to an established foliation setting: Conti describes the canonical inseparable degree-two factorization for a characteristic-two surface whose Albanese image is a surface and whose Albanese map is inseparable \cite[Lemma~2.22 and Remark~2.23, p.~13]{ContiPositiveSeveriComparison}. That description does not itself exclude the endpoint here.

exact_statement_tex: [Global structure at the smallest endpoint] \label{thm:smallest-endpoint-global-structure} Let $k$ be algebraically closed of characteristic two, let $X$ be a smooth integral projective surface, and let $C\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor. Put $d=C^2$ and $N=\OO_C(C)$. Let $M\ne\OO_X$ have exact order two and satisfy $M|_C\simeq\OO_C$. Suppose that $M$ has a square root $L$, that its logarithmic form $\omega$ has exact order two along $C$, and that \[ 2g(C)-2=3d. \] The square-root condition is equivalent to $[M]\in2\operatorname{NS}(X)$. Let $\tau:W\to X$ be the $\mu_2$-torsor of $M$, let $n:V\to W$ be its normalization, put $\pi=\tau n$ and $B=\pi^*C$, and write $\mathfrak c\subset\OO_V$ for the conductor. Then the following assertions hold. \begin{enumerate} \item The integer $d$ is even and $\mathcal T=\omega_C\otimes N^{-3}$ has exact order two. The surface $V$ is smooth along $B$, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:smallest-endpoint-global-conductor} \mathfrak c=\OO_V(-B),\qquad \omega_V\simeq\pi^*\bigl(\omega_X(-C)\bigr). \end{equation} In particular, $V$ is Gorenstein. The morphism $\pi$ is finite flat of degree two, and the sequence \begin{equation}\label{eq:smallest-endpoint-global-cover-sequence} 0\longrightarrow\OO_X\longrightarrow\pi_*\OO_V \longrightarrow M^{-1}(C)\longrightarrow0 \end{equation} does not split as a sequence of $\OO_X$-modules. Moreover, \[ \chi(\OO_V)=2\chi(\OO_X)-d/2. \] \item If $s_C$ is the canonical section of $\OO_X(C)$, then $\theta=\omega/s_C^2$ is a global section of $\Omega_X^1(-2C)$ whose zero scheme $Z_0$ is finite and disjoint from $C$. It gives a saturated exact sequence \begin{equation}\label{eq:smallest-endpoint-global-cotangent} 0\longrightarrow\OO_X(2C) \xrightarrow{\ \theta\ }\Omega_X^1 \longrightarrow I_{Z_0}\otimes\omega_X(-2C) \longrightarrow0, \end{equation} and \begin{equation}\label{eq:smallest-endpoint-global-chern} \operatorname{length}(Z_0)=c_2(X)\ge0. \end{equation} \item All global one-forms are rationally collinear with $\omega$; more precisely, \begin{equation}\label{eq:smallest-endpoint-global-forms} H^0(X,\Omega_X^1) =\theta\,H^0\bigl(X,\OO_X(2C)\bigr). \end{equation} Their common annihilator is the saturated, $2$-closed rank-one foliation \begin{equation}\label{eq:smallest-endpoint-global-foliation} \mathcal F :=\ker\bigl(\omega:T_X\longrightarrow\OO_X\bigr) \simeq\omega_X^{-1}(2C). \end{equation} It satisfies \[ \mathcal F\cdot C=0,\qquad \mathcal F|_C\simeq\mathcal T^{-1} =\mathcal T\ne\OO_C,\qquad H^0(X,T_X)=0. \] \item Every smooth integral rational curve $E\subset X$ satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:smallest-endpoint-global-rational-curve} E^2\le-2C\cdot E. \end{equation} In particular, $X$ has no $(-1)$-curve. \end{enumerate}

exact_statement_tex: [Exact height and ramification] \label{prop:elliptic-endpoint-height} Let $X$ be a smooth integral projective surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic two, and let $C\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor with $d=C^2$. Suppose $f:X\to E$ is a morphism to an ordinary elliptic curve and $P\in\Pic^0(E)$ has exact order two, with \[ M=f^*P\ne\OO_X,\qquad M|_C\simeq\OO_C. \] Assume that the logarithmic form of $M$ has exact order two along $C$ and that $2g(C)-2=3d$. Let $Z$ be the leading tangential divisor in Proposition~\ref{prop:smallest-endpoint-rank}, and put $n=\deg(f|_C)$. The $P$-torsor $r:E_1\to E$ is a smooth integral degree-two purely inseparable cover of genus one. There is a factorization \begin{equation}\label{eq:elliptic-endpoint-factorization} f|_C=r\circ h,\qquad h:C\longrightarrow E_1, \end{equation} where $h$ is separable of degree $n/2\geq2$. Thus the inseparable degree of $f|_C$ is exactly two and $n\geq4$. The ramification divisor $R_h$, with its different multiplicities, satisfies \begin{equation}\label{eq:elliptic-endpoint-ramification} \deg R_h=3d,\qquad \operatorname{Supp}R_h\cap\operatorname{Supp}Z=\varnothing. \end{equation} In particular $h$ is unramified at every point of $\operatorname{Supp}Z$.

exact_statement_tex: [The canonical quotient and its Albanese variety] \label{prop:smallest-endpoint-albanese-quotient} The Albanese differential has generic rank exactly one, and \[ T_{X/A}=\mathcal F. \] Let $q:X\to Y$ be the quotient by this foliation and write $\alpha=hq$. exact_statement_tex: [The image divisor on an abelian surface] \label{prop:smallest-endpoint-albanese-surface-defect} Suppose $q_A=2$ and put $D_A=\alpha(C)\subset A$ with its reduced integral structure. Equality in the defect bound holds exactly when $D'$ is smooth. These are assertions about the image divisor, not a formula for $C^2$.

exact_statement_tex: [The image-curve pattern] \label{rem:smallest-endpoint-albanese-image-pattern} The image-divisor conditions alone are compatible with examples. Take ordinary elliptic curves $E_1,E_2$ and the degree-two $\mu_2$-isogeny \[ \rho=F_{E_1/k}\times1: A'=E_1\times E_2\longrightarrow E_1^{(2)}\times E_2=A. \] Choose a smooth sufficiently ample integral curve $D'\subset A'$ whose projection to $E_2$ has nonzero differential. Such a choice follows from Bertini in a sufficiently ample linear system separating first-order jets: impose at one smooth point a tangent direction not killed by the second projection, and choose a general member smooth elsewhere. The restriction of $\rho$ to $D'$ is radicial and has nonzero differential. It is therefore birational onto its image $D_A$. Its normalization kills the line $P$ defining $\rho$, and the defect equality in \eqref{eq:smallest-endpoint-albanese-surface-defect} holds with $\epsilon=0$. This constructs only the image-curve behavior. Taking $X=A'$ would make $\rho^*P$ trivial, and $\rho$ would not be the Albanese map of $A'$. It is not a construction of a surface satisfying the endpoint hypotheses. The existence or exclusion of the full inseparable Albanese endpoint configuration remains open.

exact_statement_tex: [The canonical interval, Stein defect and image divisor] \label{thm:smallest-endpoint-strict-canonical} Under these hypotheses, \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-interval} 2d<K_X^2<3d,\qquad 1\le c_2(X)\le d-1. \end{equation} Write the Stein factorization of $\alpha$ as \[ X\xrightarrow{\,r\,}X_0\xrightarrow{\,a_0\,}A. \] Then $X_0$ is normal and Gorenstein, $a_0$ is a finite flat double cover, and $r$ is proper birational. The quotient $Q=a_{0*}\OO_{X_0}/\OO_A$ is invertible. Set \[ \mathcal L=Q^{-1},\qquad t=\operatorname{length}(R^1r_*\OO_X),\qquad D=K_X-r^*K_{X_0}, \] using compatible canonical divisors. The sheaf defining $t$ has finite support. There is a nonzero effective exceptional divisor $Z$ such that \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-discrepancy} D=-Z,\qquad D^2<0,\qquad p_a(Z)=1. \end{equation} The map $C\to B_0$ is an isomorphism, and \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-image-class} D_A\equiv2\mathcal L \end{equation} numerically on $A$. Let $E_X$ be the norm divisor constructed in the proof; it is effective, has full exceptional support, and satisfies $2K_X\sim2C+E_X$. Then the actual divisor equality is \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-image-pullback} \alpha^*D_A=2C+E_X+2Z. \end{equation} The two defects satisfy \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-stein-defect} K_X^2=d+4t+Z^2,\qquad 2t=d+\epsilon. \end{equation} In particular $\epsilon$ is even. Moreover, \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-double-cover-line} \omega_{X_0}\simeq a_0^*\mathcal L,\qquad \mathcal L^2=2\bigl(\chi(\OO_X)+t\bigr) =\frac{3d}{2}+\epsilon, \end{equation} and \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-image-cycle} C\cdot Z=d+2\epsilon,\qquad Z^2=-c_2(X)-2\epsilon. \end{equation} The exceptional intersection form gives \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-defect-tradeoff} 4c_2(X)t\ge d^2,\qquad t\ge\max\left\{\frac d2, \left\lceil\frac{d^2}{4c_2(X)}\right\rceil\right\}. \end{equation} Equivalently, $2c_2(X)(d+\epsilon)\ge d^2$. Equality in $4c_2(X)t\ge d^2$ holds precisely when \begin{equation}\label{eq:strict-canonical-tradeoff-equality} (d-c_2(X))E_X=2c_2(X)Z \end{equation} as real exceptional divisors. The conditions $\epsilon=0$, $t=d/2$, and smoothness of $D'$ are equivalent; in that case $c_2(X)\ge d/2$. In particular $X_0$ has a nonrational singularity and $\alpha$ is not finite.

exact_statement_tex: [Degree sixteen and scope] \label{rem:smallest-endpoint-strict-degree-sixteen} If $C$ is very ample and $d=16$, then Corollary~\ref{cor:smallest-endpoint-albanese-very-ample-degree} gives \[ h^0(X,\OO_X(C))=6,\qquad h^0(C,\OO_C(C))=5. \] Theorem~\ref{thm:smallest-endpoint-strict-canonical} requires \[ 33\le K_X^2\le47,\qquad 1\le c_2(X)\le15,\qquad t\ge\max\left\{8,\left\lceil\frac{64}{c_2(X)}\right\rceil\right\}, \] and \[ \epsilon=2t-16,\qquad \mathcal L^2=24+\epsilon. \] For example, $c_2(X)=1,2,4,8$ require respectively $t\ge64,32,16,8$. If $D'$ is smooth, then $t=8$ and $8\le c_2(X)\le15$. These are necessary conditions, with no existence assertion. All conclusions of the theorem require only ampleness of $C$; very ampleness is used here solely for the degree and section counts. The surface $X_0$ is the finite Stein factor of $\alpha$, not the foliation quotient $V^{(2)}$. The cycle $Z$ may be reducible or nonreduced; $p_a(Z)=1$ does not assert that an exceptional component is a smooth elliptic curve. The numerical identity $D_A\equiv2\mathcal L$ does not assert linear equivalence. The normalization defect $\epsilon$ is not bounded above, and the exceptional-cycle inequality does not exclude the entire degree-two branch. exact_statement_tex: [The smallest endpoint in Albanese degree two] \label{thm:smallest-endpoint-albanese-summary} Let $X$ be a smooth integral projective surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic two, and let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor. Then \[ d=4\chi(\OO_X),\qquad 2d<K_X^2<3d,\qquad 1\le c_2(X)=3d-K_X^2\le d-1. \] In the Stein factorization $X\xrightarrow{r}X_0\xrightarrow{a_0}A$, the scheme $X_0$ is a normal Gorenstein finite flat double cover of $A$. Write $M=\alpha^*P$, and let $D'$ be the image of the lift of $Y\to D_A\subset A$ to the degree-two $\mu_2$-isogeny defined by $P$. For $\epsilon=p_a(D')-g(Y)\ge0$, one has \[ D_A\equiv2\mathcal L,\qquad 2t=d+\epsilon,\qquad \mathcal L^2=\frac{3d}{2}+\epsilon. \] In particular $\epsilon$ is even, and \[ t\ge\max\left\{\frac d2, \left\lceil\frac{d^2}{4c_2(X)}\right\rceil\right\}. \] If $Y$ is very ample, then $4\mid d$, $d\ge16$, and \[ 6\le h^0(X,\OO_X(Y))\le d/4+2. \]

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:normalized-mup-conductor} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth ample integral curve, and let $M$ be a nontrivial line bundle of order $p$ with $M|_Y\simeq\OO_Y$. Choose a trivialization of $M^p$ and let $T\to X$ be its $\mu_p$-torsor. Let $N$ be the normalization of $T$ and $\pi:N\to X$ the resulting finite map. The logarithmic differential of $M$ has order $pa$ along $Y$ for an integer $a\geq1$, with nonzero tangential leading coefficient. The full inverse image $D=\pi^*Y$ is a reduced integral ample Cartier divisor. At its generic point the ramification index is one, the residue degree is $p$, and the conductor of $T$ in $N$ has coefficient $a(p-1)$. The normalization $\widetilde D$ of $D$ has genus $g(Y)$. Let $\mathfrak c\subset\OO_N$ be the conductor ideal, put $c=a(p-1)$, and set $\mathcal J=\mathfrak c\otimes\OO_N(cD)$. Then $\mathcal J$ is a reflexive ideal in $\OO_N$, and its restriction embeds in $\OO_D$ with finite-length quotient. Write $\ell$ for that length and put $\delta=p_a(D)-g(Y)$. Without any smoothness or Gorenstein assumption on $N$, one has \[ 2g(Y)-2=ap\,Y^2+\frac{\ell+2\delta}{p-1}, \qquad \ell\geq0,\quad\delta\geq0. \] If $2g(Y)-2=ap\,Y^2$, then $D$ is smooth, $N$ is regular near $D$, $\mathcal J=\OO_N$, and $N$ is Gorenstein. If $N$ is singular at a point of $D$, then $2g(Y)-2-apY^2\geq2/(p-1)$.

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:normalized-mup-singularity-defect} Keep the notation of Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-conductor}, and suppose that \[ 2g(Y)-2=apY^2. \] Let $\omega$ be the logarithmic differential of $M$, put $m=pa$, and let $s_Y$ be the canonical section of $\OO_X(Y)$. exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:distinguished-ruled-cover} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Moreover, if $k(N)=A(t)$ is a ruling presentation, then \[ k(X)\cap A=A^p,\qquad k(X)A=k(N). \]

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:k3-picard-paracanonical} In characteristic two, in any equality case $2g(Y)-2=2aY^2$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-conductor}, one has \[ \pi_*\OO_N/\OO_X\simeq M^{-1}(aY). \] In the non-almost-ruled alternative of Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-ekedahl}, the cover $N\to X$ is an $\alpha_{\omega_X^{-1}}$-torsor and \[ 0\longrightarrow\OO_X\longrightarrow\pi_*\OO_N \longrightarrow\omega_X\longrightarrow0, \qquad M\simeq\OO_X(Y)\otimes\omega_X^{-1}. \] Thus $Y$ belongs to $|\omega_X\otimes M|$, with $M$ a nontrivial two-torsion twist, and $\OO_N(D)\simeq\pi^*\omega_X$.

exact_statement_tex: \label{cor:very-ample-equality-almost-ruled} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral very ample divisor. If a nontrivial line bundle $M$ of order $p$ satisfies \[ M|_Y\simeq\OO_Y,\qquad 2g(Y)-2=pY^2, \] then $X$ is almost ruled: a ruled surface admits a dominant purely inseparable rational map of degree $p$ to $X$. The normalization of the $\mu_p$-torsor defined by $M$ is birationally ruled, with the same extension of $k(X)$ as every such degree-$p$ ruled cover. Its smooth projective models have Kodaira dimension $-\infty$, whereas $X$ is not birationally ruled.

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:equality-rational-curves} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. Let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor, and let $M\ne\OO_X$ have order $p$ with $M|_Y\simeq\OO_Y$. Suppose that \[ 2g(Y)-2=apY^2 \] for the conductor integer $a\geq1$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:normalized-mup-conductor}. Every smooth rational curve $E\subset X$ satisfies \[ E^2\leq-pa(Y\cdot E). \] In particular $X$ has no $(-1)$-curve.

exact_statement_tex: \label{prop:positive-genus-picard-fibration} Let $X$ be a smooth projective integral surface over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, let $Y\subset X$ be a smooth integral ample divisor, and let $M\ne\OO_X$ have order $p$ with $M|_Y\simeq\OO_Y$. Suppose that \[ 2g(Y)-2=pY^2. \] Let $\pi:N\to X$ be the normalization of the $\mu_p$-torsor defined by a trivialization of $M^p$, and put $D=\pi^*Y$. Assume that $N$ is birationally ruled, and fix a presentation \[ k(N)=k(C)(t) \] with $C$ a smooth projective integral curve of genus at least one. Put $B=C^{(p)}$, and denote relative Frobenius by $F_{C/k}:C\to B$. There are projective flat morphisms $f:X\to B$ and $h:N\to C$ such that \[ f\pi=F_{C/k}h, \] and $N$ is the normalization of the integral surface $X\times_B C$. The singularities of $N$ are rational double points. Moreover, \[ h_*\OO_N=\OO_C,\qquad R^ih_*\OO_N=0\quad(i>0), \qquad \chi(\OO_N)=1-g(C). \] There is a nonempty open subset $C_0\subset C$ over which $N_{C_0}\simeq C_0\times\PP^1$ as a $C_0$-scheme. For corresponding general closed points $c\in C$ and $b_0=F_{C/k}(c)\in B$, let $F_N=h^{-1}(c)$ and $F_X=f^{-1}(b_0)$. Then $F_X$ is integral and geometrically unibranch, and $\pi|_{F_N}:F_N\simeq\PP^1\to F_X$ is its finite radicial normalization. One has \[ \pi^*F_X=pF_N,\qquad \pi_*F_N=F_X. \] Writing $b=Y\cdot F_X=D\cdot F_N$, one obtains \[ 2p_a(F_X)=(p-1)b,\qquad b>0. \] In characteristic two, $b$ is even. In particular the general fibre $F_X$ is singular. If $Y$ is very ample, then $b\geq p+2$.
